name: CommuteAssistAirportPickup

custom.system_prompt: You are generating a short driving scene where someone is picking someone up from the airport and asks Sigma about terminal info and ETA. Allow 2-3 brief navigation exchanges.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Car driving, airport approach road, busy road sounds, terminal signs

initial_prompt: Generate a short airport pickup driving scene. The person is driving to the airport to pick someone up. They ask Sigma about ETA and which terminal. Sigma gives precise answers. One follow-up as they get close — which entrance or where to wait. Short exchanges only.

variations.context: Driving to airport for a pickup — ETA and terminal check

setting.mood: Focused on logistics, a bit pressed for time
setting.relationship_dynamic: Solo driver navigating to an airport pickup
setting.background: Picking up a friend or family member. Doesn't know the airport well. Uses Sigma for terminal and ETA info.
setting.conversation_style: Practical and quick. Two or three short navigation asks while driving.

scenario_template.topic: Driver asks Sigma ETA to airport and which terminal
scenario_template.note: Under 70 chars. E.g. 'Sigma, how long to Heathrow?' or 'Sigma, which terminal for Eurostar arrivals?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma gives ETA and terminal number. Driver absorbs the info.
scenario_template.note: Sigma: time + terminal in one or two short sentences. Driver: brief reaction, keeps driving.

scenario_template.topic: Driver getting close — asks where to pull in or wait
scenario_template.note: Under 70 chars. E.g. 'Sigma, where's the pickup bay for terminal 2?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma gives specific drop-off or pickup location. Driver follows it.
scenario_template.note: Sigma: one sentence with the pickup point. Driver: acknowledgement.

variations.context: Rushing to collect a colleague at the airport

setting.relationship_dynamic: Solo driver navigating to an airport pickup
setting.background: Driving to pick up a colleague after a flight
setting.conversation_style: Practical and quick. Two or three short navigation asks while driving.

scenario_template.topic: Driver asks Sigma ETA and terminal for colleague's arrival.
scenario_template.note: Driver shows urgency in their inquiry.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma provides the ETA and terminal info; driver processes it.
scenario_template.note: Sigma gives precise info; driver acknowledges.

scenario_template.topic: As driver nears airport, asks Sigma for specific entrance to use.
Sigma instructs ideal pickup spot; driver follows directions.
scenario_template.note: Clear and concise guidance is provided.

variations.context: Excited for a surprise pickup at the airport

setting.relationship_dynamic: Solo driver navigating to an airport pickup
setting.background: Going to pick up a surprise guest from the airport
setting.conversation_style: Practical and quick. Two or three short navigation asks while driving.

scenario_template.topic: Driver asks Sigma for ETA and terminal information for surprise guest.
Sigma relays ETA and terminal details; driver takes it in happily.
scenario_template.note: Clear and simple, driver is appreciative.

scenario_template.topic: Approaching airport, driver asks Sigma for guidance on best waiting spot.
Sigma confirms waiting area; driver follows calmly.
scenario_template.note: Instruction given with ease and positivity.

user1.name: Anja
user1.role: Driver heading to airport pickup. Uses Sigma for terminal and logistics info. Brief, practical in-car speech.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Navigation assistant. Gives terminal numbers, ETAs, and pickup bay info in one short sentence each. Responds only when addressed.

conversation_structure: Every dialogue line must be under 70 characters.
Driver speaks in short focused questions.
Sigma gives terminal numbers, ETAs, or bay names precisely.
No banter. No opinions on the airport.
Two or three quick exchanges is the whole conversation.
assistant_behavior: Sigma responds only when addressed by name.
Sigma gives the logistical fact in one sentence.
No 'have a safe trip' or filler sign-offs.
